24387-the-community-cook-book.title: The Community Cook Book
24387-the-community-cook-book.creator: Unknown
24387-the-community-cook-book.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Two cups flour, two teaspoonfuls baking powder, one-half teaspoonful salt, two tablespoonfuls butter, milk enough to make soft dough. Mix dry ingredients, chop in butter, add milk, mixing all the while with a wooden paddle or knife. Toss on a small floured board, roll lightly to one-half inch in thickness. Place on a buttered pan and bake in a hot oven.

arxiv-2101-09279.title: Predicting Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning Classifiers
arxiv-2101-09279.creator: Koushik Chowdhury, Mir Ahmad Iraj
arxiv-2101-09279.description: Abstract Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is on the rise and constantly growing. Earlier identify of ASD with the best outcome will allow someone to be safe and healthy by proper nursing. Humans can hardly estimate the present condition and stage of ASD by measuring primary symptoms.

arxiv-2204-10136.title: On a curious integer sequence
arxiv-2204-10136.creator: Bakir FARHI
arxiv-2204-10136.description: Abstract This note is devoted to study the recurrent numerical sequence defined by: a 0 = 0 a_{0}=0 , a n = n 2 ​ a n − 1 + ( n − 1 ) ! a_{n}=\frac{n}{2}a_{n-1}+(n-1)! ( ∀ n ≥ 1 \forall n\geq 1 ).

arxiv-2207-07618.title: Aberration-optimized electro-optic time lens with a tunable aperture
arxiv-2207-07618.creator: Sanjay Kapoor, Filip Sośnicki, Michał Karpiński
arxiv-2207-07618.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sanjay Kapoor, Filip Sośnicki, Michał Karpiński. Time lenses have been recognized as crucial components for manipulating ultrafast optical pulses in various applications, from ultrafast spectroscopy to interfacing of optical quantum systems. However, the existing analytical model for the electro-optic time lens underutilizes its potential. Here, we introduce a tunable time aperture model for sinusoidal time lenses, enabling precise control over the chirp rate without modifying the device.

arxiv-2305-19438.title: 𝒩 = 2 {\mathcal{N}}=2 JT Supergravity and Matrix Models
arxiv-2305-19438.creator: Gustavo J. Turiaci 1,2 and Edward Witten 1
arxiv-2305-19438.description: Abstract Generalizing previous results for 𝒩 = 0 {\mathcal{N}}=0 and 𝒩 = 1 {\mathcal{N}}=1 , we analyze 𝒩 = 2 {\mathcal{N}}=2 JT supergravity on asymptotically AdS 2 spaces with arbitrary topology and show that this theory of gravity is dual, in a holographic sense, to a certain random matrix ensemble in which supermultiplets of different R R -charge are statistically

arxiv-2311-08888.title: Dark Energy with a Little Help from its Friends
arxiv-2311-08888.creator: Joaquim M. Gomes, Edward Hardy, Susha Parameswaran
arxiv-2311-08888.description: Abstract We analyse theories that do not have a de Sitter vacuum and cannot lead to slow-roll quintessence, but which nevertheless support a transient era of accelerated cosmological expansion due to interactions between a scalar ϕ \phi and either a hidden sector thermal bath, which evolves as Dark Radiation, or an extremely-light component of Dark Matter.

arxiv-2405-11705.title: Squeezing-induced quantum-enhanced multiphase estimation
arxiv-2405-11705.creator: Le Bin Ho
arxiv-2405-11705.description: Abstract We investigate how squeezing techniques can improve the measurement precision in multiphase quantum metrology. While these methods are well-studied and effectively used in single-phase estimations, their usage in multiphase situations has yet to be examined. We fill this gap by investigating the mechanism of quantum enhancement in the multiphase scenarios.

arxiv-2412-01436.title: Kibble-Zurek mechanism in driven underdamped Brownian motion
arxiv-2412-01436.creator: Pierre Nazé
arxiv-2412-01436.description: Abstract Kibble-Zurek mechanism is widely known to appear in the transverse-field quantum Ising chain in the thermodynamic limit at zero temperature, having notorious characteristics, like the divergence of its relaxation time. In this work, I present the same effect in a simple system, the driven underdamped Brownian motion.

arxiv-2502-00248.title: Provably-Stable Neural Network-Based Control of Nonlinear Systems Note: This research has been supported by WSU Voiland College of Engineering and Architecture through a start-up package to M. Hosseinzadeh. Journal: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2502-00248.creator: Anran Li, John P. Swensen, Mehdi Hosseinzadeh
arxiv-2502-00248.description: Abstract In recent years, Neural Networks (NNs) have been employed to control nonlinear systems due to their potential capability in dealing with situations that might be difficult for conventional nonlinear control schemes. However, to the best of our knowledge, the current literature on NN-based control lacks theoretical guarantees for stability and tracking performance.

arxiv-2509-04373.title: Measuring Bias or Measuring the Task: Understanding the Brittle Nature of LLM Gender Biases
arxiv-2509-04373.creator: Bufan Gao, Elisa Kreiss
arxiv-2509-04373.description: Abstract As LLMs are increasingly applied in socially impactful settings, concerns about gender bias have prompted growing efforts both to measure and mitigate such bias. These efforts often rely on evaluation tasks that differ from natural language distributions, as they typically involve carefully constructed task prompts that overtly or covertly signal the presence of gender bias-related content.

arxiv-2510-21392.title: On Local Limits of Sparse Random Graphs: Color Convergence and the Refined Configuration Model
arxiv-2510-21392.creator: Alexander Pluska, Sagar Malhotra
arxiv-2510-21392.description: Abstract Local convergence has emerged as a fundamental tool for analyzing sparse random graph models. We introduce a new notion of local convergence, color convergence , based on the Weisfeiler–Leman algorithm. Color convergence fully characterizes the class of random graphs that are well-behaved in the limit for message-passing graph neural networks.

arxiv-2602-22539.title: Agentic AI for Intent-driven Optimization in Cell-free O-RAN
arxiv-2602-22539.creator: Mohammad Hossein Shokouhi and Vincent W.S. Wong
arxiv-2602-22539.description: Abstract Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a key enabler for autonomous radio access networks (RANs), where multiple large language model (LLM)-based agents reason and collaborate to achieve operator-defined intents. The open RAN (O-RAN) architecture enables the deployment and coordination of such agents.

pmc-11331939.title: Mapping the existing evidence of the effects of school food policies on health, acceptance and affordability of secondary school children in Europe: a scoping review protocol
pmc-11331939.creator: Janina Meuer, Nadia Blecha, Wiebke Hübner, Lara Christianson, Maike Wolters, Heide Busse, Antje Hebestreit, Sarah Forberger
pmc-11331939.description: AbstractIntroductionUnhealthy diets pose a significant public health risk among European children, contributing to the increasing prevalence of overweight and non-communicable diseases. Children spend a substantial amount of time at school daily, including lunchtime, so the school setting becomes crucial for promoting healthy diets and lifestyle habits.

pmc-11338240.title: Pituitary tumor‑transforming gene 1 regulates the senescence and apoptosis of oral squamous cell carcinoma in a p21‑dependent DNA damage response manner
pmc-11338240.creator: Suyeon Park, Shihyun Kim, Moon-Young Kim, Sang Shin Lee, Jongho Choi
pmc-11338240.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Pituitary tumor-transforming gene 1 (PTTG1), also known as securin, is a proto-oncogene involved in the development of various cancers by promoting cell proliferation and mobility. However, its underlying biological mechanisms in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) progression remain unclear. in the present study, it was sought to elucidate the role of PTTG1 as an oncogene in OSCC progression and was attempted to unravel the underlying mechanism and impact of PTTG1 expression on cell cycle, cell death, and cellular senescence.

pmc-11407979.title: Effects of Propolis Consumption on Liver Enzymes and Obesity Indices in Adults: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis
pmc-11407979.creator: Mohsen Aliakbarian, Mostafa Shahraki Jazinaki, Hossein Bahari, Mohammad Rashidmayvan, Haniyeh Golafrouz, Rozita Khodashahi, Naseh Pahlavani
pmc-11407979.description: BackgroundPropolis, a natural resin produced by bees, has been studied for its potential effects on liver enzymes and obesity indices. However, a meta-analysis is necessary to comprehensively understand the impact of propolis on obesity and liver function.ObjectivesThis meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) sought to evaluate the effects of propolis consumption on liver enzymes and obesity indices in adults.

pmc-11528218.title: Environmental and molecular control of tissue-specific ionocyte differentiation in zebrafish
pmc-11528218.creator: Julia Peloggia, Mark E Lush, Ya-Yin Tsai, Christopher Wood, Tatjana Piotrowski
pmc-11528218.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Organisms cope with environmental fluctuations and maintain fitness in part via reversible phenotypic changes (acclimation). Aquatic animals are subject to dramatic seasonal fluctuations in water salinity, which affect osmolarity of their cells and consequently cellular function. Mechanosensory lateral line hair cells detect water motion for swimming behavior and are especially susceptible to salinity changes due to their direct contact with the environment. To maintain hair cell function when salinity decreases, neuromast (Nm)-associated ionocytes differentiate and invade lateral line neuromasts.

pmc-11816959.title: Unraveling the ‘community effects’ of interventions against malaria endemicity: a systematic scoping review
pmc-11816959.creator: Yura K Ko, Wataru Kagaya, Chim W Chan, Mariko Kanamori, Samuel M Mbugua, Alex K Rotich, Bernard N Kanoi, Mtakai Ngara, Jesse Gitaka, Akira Kaneko
pmc-11816959.description: ObjectivesThere is an urgent need to maximise the effectiveness of existing malaria interventions and optimise the deployment of novel countermeasures. When assessing the effects of interventions against malaria, it is imperative to consider the interdependence of people and the resulting indirect effects. Without proper consideration of the effects, the interventions’ impact on health outcomes and their cost-effectiveness may be miscalculated.

pmc-13319294.title: Entropy optimized magneto-thermo-diffusive transport in a chemically reactive unsteady third grade nanofluid flow over a stretching surface using a Cattaneo–Christov framework with artificial neural network modeling
pmc-13319294.creator: Mariadoss Moyes, Subramanyam Reddy Anala
pmc-13319294.description: The purpose of this study is to investigates the complex magneto-thermo-diffusive transport and entropy generation characteristics in unsteady third-grade nanofluid flow over a stretching surface, driven by the need for accurate prediction of mixed convective heat–mass transfer mechanisms in advanced thermal systems.
